canonical_question: Why does the as-cast sample oxidized at 850 °C exhibit a mixed oxide layer while the ultrafine-grained sample forms a Cr2O3 layer followed by Al2O3 at the same temperature?

question_variants.question: Why does the as-cast sample oxidized at 850 °C exhibit a mixed oxide layer while the ultrafine-grained sample forms a Cr2O3 layer followed by Al2O3 at the same temperature?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The difference in oxide layer composition is attributed to the microstructure: the as-cast sample forms mixed Cr-, Fe-, and Co-rich oxides with minor Al2O3, while the ultrafine-grained sample forms a protective Cr2O3 layer followed by an Al2O3 layer due to enhanced GB diffusion.

answers.answer: The as-cast sample exhibits mixed oxides (Cr, Fe, Co-rich) with minor Al2O3, whereas the ultrafine-grained sample forms a thin Cr2O3 layer followed by aluminum-rich inner oxides, driven by higher grain boundary density facilitating protective scale formation.
answers.mechanism: enhanced GB diffusion in ultrafine grains promotes Cr and Al oxidation
evidence_spans: In the current work, microstructural refinement of the AlCoCrFeNi HEA was accomplished via severe surface deformation using stationary friction processing (SFP). The processing resulted in ultrafine-grain structure with a significant fraction of nanograins in the as-cast HEA along with significant elemental homogenization. The processed HEA samples demonstrated exceptional oxidation resistance, and the reported mass gain values are among the lowest for the investigated HEA. The remarkable performance of the processed HEAs was attributed to the formation of an intact, dense, uniformly distributed oxide scale, favored by large grain boundary density, higher surface free energy, and uniform elemental distribution.

source_evidence_spans: As-cast sample oxidized at 850 °C exhibits an oxide layer comprising Cr-, Fe-, and Co-rich oxides with a minor amount of Al 2 O 3 . However, the oxide layer formed on the surface of ultrafine-grained samples oxidized at 850 °C consists of a thin Cr 2 O 3 layer followed by aluminum-rich inner oxides.
